condition: Claudin 18.2-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma
indication_tracked: First-line treatment in combination with fluoropyrimidine- and platinum-based chemotherapy

eu.jca_note: Not in EU JCA scope: the EU application was filed before the EU HTA Regulation applied (12 January 2025).
eu.epar_summary:
Vyloy is a cancer medicine that is used to treat adults with gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (a type of cancer of the stomach or the transition between the stomach and oesophagus).

It is used in combination with chemotherapy when the cancer is locally advanced (has spread nearby) and cannot be removed by surgery or when it is metastatic (has spread to other parts of the body). Vyloy can be used when the cancer cells are HER2 negative and Claudin (CLDN) 18.2 positive; this means they do not have large quantities of the HER2 receptor (target) on their surface but do have a large number of the CLDN18.2 protein.

Gastric and gastro-oesophageal adenocarcinoma are rare, and Vyloy was designated an ‘orphan medicine’ (a medicine used in rare diseases) on 26 November 2010.

Vyloy contains the active substance zolbetuximab.

DE.outcome_short: Indication of minor added benefit (PD-L1 CPS <1) · not proven (CPS ≥1)
DE.opinion: New full assessment after the orphan-drug revenue threshold was exceeded. PD-L1 CPS <1: indication (Anhaltspunkt) of a minor added benefit vs CAPOX. PD-L1 CPS ≥1: added benefit not proven. (The first decision of 17 Apr 2025 treated it as an orphan drug, with added benefit deemed proven by the authorisation.)
DE.comparator: CPS ≥1: pembrolizumab or nivolumab (CPS ≥5) + chemotherapy. CPS <1: fluoropyrimidine/platinum-based chemotherapy
DE.reimbursement: Reimbursed by statutory health insurance (GKV); price negotiated with GKV-Spitzenverband.
